title: Open-ended innovation in zero-sum games
abstract: This note discusses zero-sum games with open-ended innovation, whereby each player may introduce new strategies. The innovation process is modelled as a draw of new strategies form a distribution. It is argued that, under generic conditions, this setting can lead to an everlasting innovation arm race, because the introduction of new technologies of one player increases the marginal utility for technological innovation of the opponent.
summary: This theoretical note examines zero-sum games where players can continuously innovate by introducing new strategies. It models this process mathematically and concludes that if the cost of innovation is low, the system enters an everlasting 'arm race.' This continuous competition ultimately drives the achievable payoffs toward zero.
main_problem: The paper analyzes zero-sum games where players can introduce new strategies, investigating whether this process leads to an endless cycle of innovation.
main_result: Under generic conditions and low innovation costs, the system predicts an everlasting innovation arm race, leading to vanishingly small payoffs for both players in the limit of infinite strategies.
method: The analysis uses mathematical modeling based on large random zero-sum games, employing derivatives to examine how marginal payoff changes with increasing strategy sets.
model_or_system: The model is a two-player zero-sum game defined by a payoff function $\pi(s_1, s_2)$, where strategies are probability distributions over a simplex. The analysis focuses on the large limit of the number of available strategies ($n_1, n_2$).
key_observables: The value of the game $V(n_1, n_2)$ and the function $u(x)$ characterizing its dependence on the strategy ratio $x=n_1/n_2$.
important_parameters: Innovation costs ($c_1, c_2$) and the limit where these costs approach zero.
main_assumptions: The setting assumes generic conditions for open-ended innovation and relies on modeling strategy expansion as adding dimensions to the payoff matrix.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates $V$ versus $n_1$ for fixed $n_2$, with an inset showing $u(x)$ plotted against $\sqrt{x}$, highlighting concavity.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the mathematical framework of open-ended zero-sum games, derives approximations for the game value in large limits, and then analyzes the condition for sustained innovation by balancing marginal gains against costs.
why_interesting: While focused on game theory, the concept of diminishing returns and resource depletion due to continuous technological advancement mirrors concepts studied in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics or complex adaptive systems.
